Shear key (heel, b = 0.5 m, d = 0.5 m): passive resistance on the front face with Rankine K_p; vertical stress starts at the front ground (front fill + foundation γ); reduction factor 0.5 (same as FS_p = 2 in the METU CE366 example); reduced by (1−k_v)K_PE/K_P in the seismic case. Key passive counts regardless of the toe-passive setting; if the front soil may be removed by excavation or scour, enter embedment D = 0 (Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (taban dişi, D1 = D + diş derinliği); ODTÜ CE366 Recitation 5 P1 (P_p = 65D + 32.5D², FS_p = 2))

Sliding is checked on two surfaces: the base interface (V tanδ_b + c_a·B′ + key passive) and the horizontal plane through the key tip ((ΣV + soil weight beside the key) tanφ + c·B′ + key passive). On the key-tip plane the thrust on the heel line is extended to the key bottom (foundation K_a, δ = β; surcharge, water and seismic increments and the inertia of the soil beside the key included). The smaller ratio governs. With an undrained foundation, seismic loading or sloping backfill, the key-zone thrust cannot be computed; the analysis stops with an explicit error (Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (taban dişi, D1 = D + diş derinliği); ODTÜ CE366 Recitation 5 P1 (P_p = 65D + 32.5D², FS_p = 2))

Key depth is not added to the bearing embedment (conservative in every case); only shear and moment demands are given for the key (V = unreduced static passive, M = V·arm); no reinforced-concrete design (Koordinatör kararı; tutucu)

Global stability is computed without the key: the Bishop circle passes below the base and the key volume is treated as soil. The strength side is conservative (concrete is stronger than soil); the neglected concrete-soil weight difference has a small effect (Koordinatör kararı; tutucu)
